The Live Demo Floor

The Machines
Are The Event.

The demo floor is not an exhibition hall. It is a curated showcase of working autonomous systems operating in real time — the only place in the world where you can walk between 40+ live robots in a single afternoon.

Company names below are illustrative of the categories and technologies represented on the demo floor and do not represent confirmed exhibitors. Confirmed companies will be announced soon.

Humanoid Systems
Figure AI, Agility Robotics, 1X Technologies, Apptronik, and Unitree on an open floor.
Industrial & Warehouse
Robotic arms, AMRs, picking systems and conveyor AI from ABB, Fanuc, KUKA, Siemens, Amazon Robotics.
Autonomous Vehicles
Self-driving platforms, last-mile delivery robots, drone systems from Waymo, Zipline, Skydio.
Surgical & Medical
Robotic surgery, AI-guided diagnostics, rehabilitation robotics. Intuitive Surgical, CMR Surgical, Moon Surgical.
AI Infrastructure
Edge AI chips, robotics processors, simulation platforms. NVIDIA Jetson & Thor, Qualcomm, ARM, Hailo.
Sensors & Perception
LiDAR, vision systems, tactile sensors, depth cameras, sensor fusion. Velodyne, Ouster, Luminar.
Agricultural Robotics
Autonomous harvesting robots, crop inspection drones, AI-guided irrigation. John Deere, Syngenta.
Digital Twin & Simulation
Robot training simulation, synthetic data, real-time digital twin environments. NVIDIA Omniverse.
Drones & UAV Systems
Industrial inspection, logistics delivery, airspace management and autonomous aerial systems. Zipline, Skydio, Percepto.
Defence & Dual-Use
Autonomous systems where industrial and military robotics converge. Ground robots, surveillance, contested-environment autonomy.
The Moment

Why Now.

Six forces have converged simultaneously. Physical AI is not a future category — it is a present deployment challenge for every major enterprise on earth.

01
Capital Has Arrived
$16.2B into Prometheus. $675M into Figure AI. The largest funds in the world are writing their largest cheques into Physical AI.
02
Hardware Is Ready
Humanoids, cobots, drones and autonomous vehicles have crossed the reliability threshold for commercial deployment in controlled environments.
03
Models Can Act
Vision-language-action (VLA) models now allow AI to see, understand and act in the physical world — not just process text and images.
04
Enterprise Is Buying
The procurement conversation has shifted from "should we?" to "how do we scale?" Logistics, manufacturing and construction are deploying now.
05
Talent Is Concentrating
London, Oxford and Cambridge have become Europe’s defining Physical AI talent corridor. Wayve, DeepMind, Prometheus — all here.
06
No Ecosystem Platform Exists
No event brings together the capital, founders and enterprise buyers of Physical AI in one room. That is the gap the Physical AI Expo fills.
Location

Why London.

McKinsey identifies three European deep-tech hubs: Paris, the Alpine region (Zurich–Munich), and the London–Oxford–Cambridge triangle. London is the bridge point of that triangle — and the capital of Physical AI.

Project Prometheus
Kings Cross HQ. $38B valuation. Jeff Bezos chose London for one of three global headquarters of the most valuable Physical AI company in the world.
DeepMind & OpenAI
Both global AI leaders have established major London operations. The city has become the default European base for frontier AI research and deployment.
Oxford & Cambridge
Europe’s deepest robotics and AI talent pipeline. The London–Oxford–Cambridge triangle is McKinsey’s designated European deep-tech corridor.
Wayve
London-born autonomous driving company backed by SoftBank and Microsoft. One of the most advanced embodied AI companies operating on public roads today.
Ocado & Amazon Robotics
Both operating live Physical AI deployments at scale in the UK right now. Not pilots — production. The enterprise case is already proven here.
ExCeL London
The only UK venue with sufficient floor space to host 40+ live autonomous systems alongside a full conference programme in one building.

Terminology

What Is Physical AI.

Physical AI is what happens when artificial intelligence leaves the screen and enters the physical world. Instead of only processing text, images or data, physical AI systems perceive their surroundings, reason about them in real time, and act — while adapting their behaviour as conditions change, rather than following a fixed, pre-programmed script.

That’s a progression from language models to vision-language models to vision-language-action (VLA) models: AI that can now see, understand and act. These systems train in simulation, cycling data between digital twins and the real world, before that intelligence is deployed to physical hardware — including humanoids, autonomous mobile robots, drones, quadrupeds, manipulator arms and autonomous vehicles.
